description: Heritage did-you-mean tie-break (issue #668, slice H3): when an unknown command ties on Levenshtein distance between a full canonical name and a short Heritage alias that are BOTH optional-profile, the full name wins per spec/error-model.md:147-148 ('full canonical names over short aliases'). Here `dca` is distance 2 from both the Data primitive `dict` and the Heritage alias `cs`; with Data and Heritage both active the Core-beats-optional rung cannot separate them, so the alias-deprioritization rung must pick `dict`, never `cs`. This proves Heritage adds no observably-preferred short spelling to the suggestion ordering.
